look_here_first: LOOK FIRST at mature spikelets and the culm base: spikelets usually FLATTENED with relatively long DECIDUOUS floral scales, typically 3.2–4.5 mm, and a cormlike thickened culm base. Contrast odoratus mature corky rachilla that breaks into one-fruited units.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Texas native at state level under reviewed FNA/POWO concept. BONAP/NAPA target-zone three-county native proof not yet independently verified.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial flatsedge of wet or disturbed soils, with leaflike bracts radiating beneath the flower cluster.
morphology_keys.base: Cormlike swollen basal region is supporting character; photograph excavated plant without losing the base.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Terminal compound umbrella-like cluster with rays and leaflike bracts, relatively straw-colored radiating flattened spikelets.
morphology_keys.spikelets: Flattened, floral scales commonly 3.2–4.5(–6) mm and DECIDUOUS; mature fruits and exposed rachilla needed to distinguish odoratus.
morphology_keys.fruit: One achene under each fertile scale. Three stigma branches can help support the key, but use entire mature specimen.

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. odoratus mature spikelet is more subcylindrical and rachilla disarticulates into corky one-fruited segments. C. strigosus retains a cormlike base and deciduous larger scales; immature heads overlap.
comparisons.cautions: C. stenolepis is a synonym under the selected concept; do not split an extra canonical card. Maturity, anatomy and county nativity need independent verification.
